category: Category B — Tenant and Landlord Disputes
name: ₹30,000 deposit with ₹15,000 painting deduction
expected: Explains normal wear and tear doctrine (Section 108 TPA); painting cannot be arbitrarily deducted without explicit clause.
prompt: My landlord returned only ₹15,000 out of ₹30,000 deposit, deducting ₹15,000 for full flat painting. Is this legal?
raw_response:
Hello! I understand your concern, and I am here to help you resolve this unfair deduction.

### | Your Situation
You recently vacated a rented flat where your landlord returned only ₹15,000 out of your ₹30,000 security deposit, arbitrarily deducting ₹15,000 for full flat painting. This dispute over deposit retention involves your landlord in India.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108(m) and (o), a tenant is bound to restore the property in as good a condition as it was at the start, subject only to "reasonable wear and tear." A landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine painting unless explicitly agreed upon in a written contract.
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state tenancy laws) Section 11 and Section 13, security deposits must be refunded upon taking over vacant possession after making only valid, mutually agreed deductions. Arbitrary charges for standard maintenance or full repainting without contractual backing are legally invalid.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your original lease agreement, receipts of security deposit payment, handover inspection photos, and WhatsApp or email communications regarding the deposit refund.
2. Send a written demand notice to your landlord granting 15 days to refund the remaining ₹15,000, citing the relevant provisions of the Transfer of Property Act.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as the local Rent Authority or Consumer Commission, if the landlord fails to respond within the stipulated notice period.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Was there a written tenancy agreement, and did it contain any specific clause regarding mandatory painting deductions upon vacating?
2. How long did you stay in the apartment, and was the property damaged beyond normal usage?

citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
